title: Restriction-compatible bilinear multiplication on successive ideal-power quotients
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $I$ its quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Put $B_r=I^r/I^{r+1}$ with projections $\pi_r$, as in [def-weil-pbc-formal-kernel-graded-pieces]. There exist $\mathcal O_X(U)$-bilinear maps $\mu_{m,n,U}:B_m(U)\times B_n(U)\to B_{m+n}(U)$ for all natural numbers $m,n$ and opens $U$, compatible with restriction to smaller opens. For every $a\in I^m(U)$ and $b\in I^n(U)$ there is $c\in I^{m+n}(U)$ whose inclusion in $\mathcal O_X(U)$ is the product of the inclusions of $a,b$, and $\mu_{m,n,U}(\pi_m(a),\pi_n(b))=\pi_{m+n}(c)$. No algebra laws or unit are part of this statement.

source.place: Lemma 087Z (lemma-graded-module), the associated graded algebra in the statement; construction expanded from affine tensor and quotient descriptions in Schemes Tags 01I8 and 01IC. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087Z and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01IC.

proof.text: On every affine open identify the positive power section ranges with ideal powers and the quotient sections with their module quotients, using the affine product/quotient theorem. For degree zero the power inclusion is the identity. Products land in degree m+n; changing representatives by the next ideal powers changes their product by the next ideal power. Thus multiplication descends bilinearly.

Inclusions, quotient projections and ring multiplication commute with restrictions. Locally lift both quotient sections on affine covers and glue the independent local products; check equality on affine refinements of overlaps. The sheaf condition gives unique glued sections. This proves bilinearity and naturality. For actual power sections, the ring product locally lifts to the target power inclusion. That inclusion is monic by induction on ideal powers, so the lifts agree and glue to c. The quotient identity holds locally and hence globally. Empty opens, the zero and unit ideals, and zero degrees follow by the same argument.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 087Z, construction of its associated graded algebra; affine descent and representative-independence expanded from the parent node, retaining its route.

theorem formalAssociatedGraded_multiplication_exists {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    ∃ mu : ∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens),
      (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I m).val.obj (op U) →ₗ[Γ(X, U)]
        (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I n).val.obj (op U) →ₗ[Γ(X, U)]
          (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I (m + n)).val.obj (op U),
      (∀ (m n : ℕ) (U V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U)
        (a : (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I m).val.obj (op U))
        (b : (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I n).val.obj (op U)),
        (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I (m + n)).val.map (homOfLE h).op (mu m n U a b) =
          mu m n V ((formalAssociatedGradedPiece I m).val.map (homOfLE h).op a)
            ((formalAssociatedGradedPiece I n).val.map (homOfLE h).op b)) ∧
      (∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
        (a : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op U))
        (b : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).1.val.obj (op U)),
        ∃ c : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι (m + n)).1.val.obj (op U),
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι (m + n)).2.val.app (op U) c =
            (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) a)) *
              (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2.val.app (op U) b)) ∧
          mu m n U ((formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op U) a)
            ((formalAssociatedGradedπ I n).val.app (op U) b) =
              (formalAssociatedGradedπ I (m + n)).val.app (op U) c)
